Looking at the quotation, the specific mechanism is: **community-based family support hubs (Best Start Family Hubs) providing integrated early years services — parenting, feeding, financial, housing advice — legislated and delivered through local authorities**.

This is primarily about integrated welfare/family support provision for young families, not education per se (though early years is mentioned, the substance is multi-service community hubs). The closest match is welfare program provision through government policy.

Checking I38 — "Government Policy • Provision and Effects of Welfare Programs" — this fits well: the hubs are a government-mandated welfare provision program for families, being cemented in law, with local authority accountability.

I28 (Education Government Policy) could apply given the "early years as part of education system" framing, but the substance of what's described — feeding support, parenting support, financial advice, housing advice, all in one place — is welfare provision, not education delivery.
